tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent/symptoms (e.g., 'traffic is leaving the region', 'not using my local Direct Connect'), explicitly lists trigger contexts covering multiple AWS networking constructs, and even accounts for symptom-based phrasing without naming the domain directly. It is a dense but bounded paragraph, consistent with the complexity of the domain it covers.
tests.evidence: 'Use this skill when the user wants to know which path AWS will pick for their traffic, why traffic took an unexpected route, or how to make AWS prefer a path. ... Use it even when the user only describes a symptom, such as "traffic is leaving the region", "not using my local Direct Connect", "routing to the wrong VIF/location", or "path is asymmetric".'

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays focused on AWS-routing-specific domain knowledge (route evaluation orders, BGP community values, DXGW behavior) rather than explaining generic networking concepts the agent would already know.
tests.evidence: Longest prefix match first; then local preference → AS_PATH length → MED, stopping at the first difference.
